title: Topological Causal Effects
claim: Treatment changes the shape of complex outcomes, and these changes appear as shifts in topological features of their persistence diagrams.
layout: 4 panels in a row: two structures, then two diagrams; dashed highlight
description: A single horizontal strip of four panels. The left two panels show 3D ball-and-stick renderings of a macromolecule, titled 'Untreated' and 'Treated'. Atoms are colored gray, white, blue, red and yellow. The treated molecule has a different ring-like arrangement, with added red and yellow atoms. The right two panels are matching persistence diagrams, also titled 'Untreated' and 'Treated'. Each has Birth on the x-axis and Death on the y-axis, a diagonal line with a gray shaded region below it, and a +∞ line at the top. Red points mark 0-dimensional features and blue points mark 1-dimensional features, with a small legend. In the treated diagram, a dashed orange ellipse circles blue points high above the diagonal. The ellipse is where the eye goes first. It marks the new long-lived loop features that the treatment induced.
caption: Left: Example of untreated vs. treated macromolecule structures. Right: Corresponding persistence diagrams, highlighting treatment-induced changes in the 1st-order homology features.
abstract: Estimating causal effects is particularly challenging when outcomes arise in complex, non-Euclidean spaces, where conventional methods often fail to capture meaningful structural variation. We develop a framework for topological causal inference that defines treatment effects through differences in the topological structure of potential outcomes, summarized by power-weighted silhouette functions of persistence diagrams. We develop an efficient, doubly robust estimator in a fully nonparametric model, establish functional weak convergence, and construct a formal test of the null hypothesis of no topological effect. Empirical studies illustrate that the proposed method reliably quantifies topological treatment effects across diverse complex outcome types.
